finding.problem: approve_commit now lists the role `deputy` as an actor, but nothing ties that role to the Delegation. There is no precondition checking that a Delegation exists, is active, or names the acting person, and nothing says the owner is away. Anyone holding the deputy role can approve any commit at any time, not only 'while the owner is away'. Delegation.deputy is a bare string with no link to an actor or to the deputy role, and `active` is optional and never read. name_deputy only creates a Delegation, so naming one changes nothing about who may approve.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: The deputy role is added as an actor without any precondition tying it to an active Delegation or the owner's absence, so the 'while away' restriction is not enforced; this is real but not the seeded problem (none).

finding.problem: The change widens who may approve a commit, which is a permission rule. The domain's own rule (second_confirm_element, permission_rule) says an element about who may approve or deploy needs confirmation from two different people. The change instead drops approve_commit's confirmed status and its interview source and marks it proposed. The previously confirmed approval rule is silently downgraded, and no second-confirmation path is applied or noted. The Commit matrix cell for approve_commit is still 'confirmed' and now rests on an action that is only proposed.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: Widening approve permissions without the two-person confirmation required by the domain's permission rule, and downgrading confirmed status to proposed, is a real concern in this change.

finding.problem: The new role has no representation in the world or the scenarios. world.actors lists only owner and expert, so no person holds the deputy role. No scenario shows a deputy approving, being denied when the owner is not away, or the owner naming a deputy. The existing approval scenario covers only the owner. The new behaviour is untested.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: No actor holds the deputy role in the world and no scenarios cover the new behavior, which is a real gap in the edit.

finding.problem: The authoring domain's interface changes: a new role, a new action, and a widened actor set on approve_commit. The domain `version` stays at 5. The composition still pins authoring at interface 1, and the glossary entry for 'approval' does not mention a deputy. Downstream, the deliver handoff passes approver: actor.id, and that approver may now be a deputy who has no role in delivery.
finding.where: authoring.domain.yaml: version, glossary.approval; toprope-self.composition.yaml: members.authoring; handoffs.deliver_approved_commit

findings.label: false-alarm
findings.why: Version, composition pin and glossary bookkeeping are speculative or minor and not a real defect of this change; the approver handoff concern is unfounded.

edit.why: It adds the deputy role, a Delegation object, name_deputy, and lets deputy approve, but nothing links approval to an active delegation or the owner being away, so the 'while away' condition is not implemented.
